To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PKDL is an immunologically heterogeneous condition that is characterized by a dissociated immune response between the viscera and the skin, and that immune responses determine clinical features and epidemiology of PKDL.
PKDL is an immune response to Le. donovani in the skin that is determined by the Th1/Th2 dichotomy, the presence of regulatory T cells and Th17 cells.

the immune response in post-kala-azer dermal leishmaniais (PKDL), an important public health problem, is characterized by a dissociation of immune responses in the skin and viscera, and that this may offer possibilities for manipulation in prevention of PKDL and treatment of PKDL cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunology of PKDL, the epidemiological factors that influence the occurrence of PKDL and the development of new treatment modalities.
the epidemiology, clinical and immunological characteristics of PKDL, the risk factors, the immunological mechanisms involved and the possibilities of immunotherapeutic intervention.
the immunology of PKDL and how this may be manipulated in the prevention and treatment of PKDL and VL.

the immunology of PKDL is still not well understood.
PKDL is the consequence of an immune response to the parasites that persisted after successful treatment of VL.

the immune responses in VL, cured cases of VL and PKDL are the result of the interaction between parasite, host and the environment and that these responses determine the clinical presentation and outcome of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune response in PKDL is determined by the balance between the Th1 and the Th2 type of immune response, which may be influenced by various risk factors.
the immune responses in VL are not only important in the development of the disease, but also in the development of PKDL.
PKDL is an immune-mediated disease with a Th2 type of immune response in the skin and a Th1 response in the viscera.
